claims.quote: Light came through a small west window in a narrow beam that slid across trunks and splinters of packing crate.
claims.value: small west window casting a narrow beam of afternoon light

claims.quote: The mirror was where I said I would picture it: tall, walnut-framed and full-length, the glass slightly warped so the rafters bent as if they were breathing. It stood propped against the far wall, catching the slant of the afternoon.
claims.value: mirror propped against the far wall beneath a small west window

claims.quote: The trunks were stacked along the left-hand side under the rafters, one on top of another like a spine of brittle leather.
claims.value: trunks stacked along the left-hand side under the rafters

claims.quote: Nobody had been up here in years and, absurdly, the floorboards were almost clean: dustless in that particular way of places you avoid and thus never disturb.
claims.value: mirror surface never gathers dust (attic floorboards described as dustless)

Inside, on a pad of yellowing tissue, lay a small, tarnished brass locket on a fragile chain and, beside it, a larger sepia photograph folded carefully in a moth-eaten handkerchief.
claims.value: brass locket found in the largest trunk on a pad of yellowing tissue

claims.quote: The locket was colder than the air.
claims.value: locket felt cold to the touch

claims.quote: The locket was colder than the air. I pried it open with my thumbnail and found a tiny photograph of two girls pressed flat inside.
claims.value: contains tiny photograph of two girls

claims.quote: On the back of the larger photograph, when I unfolded it, someone had written a single name in faded ink: Evie.
claims.value: back of the larger photograph has 'Evie' written in faded ink

claims.quote: Decision: as a child I had never been told about Evie — the name was missing from our family stories.
claims.value: as a child, Mara had never been told about Evie

claims.quote: There, at the far end of the attic where shadow pooled behind the trunks, the glass held a second figure: a girl standing a little way from the trunks, head tilted as if listening.
claims.value: mirror reflection showed a second figure, a girl standing at the far end of the attic

claims.quote: I closed my fingers around the locket and put it in my pocket because the sensible thing was to put important things somewhere safe.

I had to force the attic open.

The hatch stuck on the second pull. My hands were already raw from hauling boxes downstairs and answering questions I did not have the patience for, so I used the crowbar the estate agent had left in the garage and pried the thing up in two impatient breaths.
claims.value: attic hatch was forced open with a crowbar by Mara
